_readme: Central product catalog for the Obi integration context (plan.md §D.1, owner decisions §D.13). This is THE single canonical registry of software products: it is the ONE place that decides which product ids exist, what role each product plays (pos | pms | accounting), and which connection types it supports — NOTHING else in the repo may define a product. It complements, never replaces, the two registries beside it: knowledge_scopes.json now holds only the reserved 'classified' label (the knowledge-scope '-test' axis was retired by ADR-0021; routing labels, validated against THIS catalog, are the content axis), and platforms.json stays the JWT-issuer registry and the valid integration-claim allow-list — this file does not duplicate it (one source per concept; the mews/toast/opera-cloud ids here intentionally equal the integration keys in platforms.json, and the loader cross-checks that). 'products' is keyed by canonical id (short lowercase slug, unique): 'label' is the display name, 'role' the product's slot role, 'aliases' alternative spellings that resolve to this id (lowercase, unique across the whole file, never colliding with any canonical id; evidence-based only — operacloud is the hyphen-free spelling of opera-cloud), 'connection_types' the §D.2-supported connection families this product can take part in. 'connection_types' (top-level) defines those families with their §D.2 flow directions; pos-pms carries both directions in ONE connection. 'legacy_aliases' maps a legacy COMPOUND claim value to the LIST of canonical ids it expands to (§D.11) — it is EMPTY by owner decision round 2 (2026-10-05, O8 closed): the only candidate, 'toast-opera', appears in no config, code, token, or tag anywhere in the repo (whole-repo search) — it existed only as plan.md's illustrative example — so no legacy compound value is real today; if one ever surfaces from a platform, add it here with its evidence. 'launch_allowlist' records the §D.13 visibility decision (Toast as POS, Mews as PMS; a FILLED pos/pms slot outside this list hides Obi, an EMPTY slot never does) — per decision round 2 (O4 closed) the allowlist gates POS/PMS ONLY: a filled accounting slot never hides Obi, it just contributes no eligibility when unsupported (unknown values still fail closed via membership). WIRED (substep 8.1.1, 2026-10-05): backend/app/platform/config/product_catalog.py loads and validates this file at startup, fail-fast on the 8 rules in docs/Final_docs/5-integration-context/catalog.md §3 (incl. the platforms.json cross-check), and exposes lookups, alias resolution and the launch allowlist; the gate consumes it in substep 8.1.3. To add a product: add one entry under 'products' following catalog.md — nothing else in the codebase defines it.
